facts.text: Visuals that work are drawings in a plan that expose dependencies and gaps rather than decorate.
facts.quote: Visuals that work are the drawings in a plan that expose dependencies and gaps, rather than decorate

facts.text: The booklet found no credible research showing that one visual format universally earns trust from engineering reviewers.
facts.quote: no credible research shows one visual format universally earns trust from engineering reviewers

facts.text: The finding that trivial graphs increase persuasion failed to replicate.
facts.quote: the finding that trivial graphs increase persuasion failed to replicate

facts.text: The booklet recommends not decorating visuals to persuade; decoration, if used at all, should aid recall.
facts.quote: do not decorate to persuade; decorate, if at all, to aid recall

facts.text: The booklet recommends dividing visual communication among six kinds: a layered roadmap, claim-to-evidence map, coverage map, architecture view, probabilistic schedule view and risk views.
facts.quote: recommends a division of labor among six kinds

facts.text: The recommended layered roadmap places time horizontally and evidence streams vertically—safety argument, model credibility, physical correlation, scenario coverage, tool chain and governance—and shows dependencies and gate diamonds rather than isolated boxes.
facts.quote: A layered roadmap: time horizontal, evidence streams vertical (safety argument, model credibility, physical correlation, scenario coverage, tool chain, governance), with dependencies and gate diamonds rather than isolated boxes.

facts.text: The recommended claim-to-evidence map tells the safety reviewer why each work package exists.
facts.quote: A claim-to-evidence map that tells the safety reviewer why each work package exists.

facts.text: The recommended coverage map places scenario or hazard dimensions on one axis and evidence source on the other, marking each cell virtual-only, virtual plus physical correlation, physical-only or uncovered.
facts.quote: A coverage map with scenario or hazard dimensions on one axis and evidence source on the other, each cell marked virtual-only, virtual plus physical correlation, physical-only or uncovered

facts.text: Uncovered cells in a coverage map must remain visibly blank rather than disappear into an "85% coverage" score.
facts.quote: uncovered cells must stay visibly blank rather than disappear into an "85% coverage" score

facts.text: The recommended architecture view shows machine, sensors, controller, environment, simulator, data stores, test oracle and comparators, marking which elements are real, modeled, emulated or substituted.
facts.quote: An architecture view showing machine, sensors, controller, environment, simulator, data stores, test oracle and comparators, marking which elements are real, modeled, emulated or substituted.

facts.text: The recommended probabilistic schedule view is a Monte Carlo S-curve with P50 and P80 marked, or a fan chart.
facts.quote: A probabilistic schedule view: a Monte Carlo S-curve with P50 and P80 marked, or a fan chart.

facts.text: The recommended risk views include a ranked top-risks table with ranges, a schedule-sensitivity tornado diagram and a risk burn-down by gate.
facts.quote: Risk views: a ranked top-risks table with ranges, a schedule-sensitivity tornado diagram and a risk burn-down by gate

facts.text: The booklet recommends including a risk heat map only for familiarity because heat maps have documented ranking defects.
facts.quote: with a heat map included only for familiarity because of its documented ranking defects

facts.text: Chapter 13 recommends a one-page credibility map and a traffic-light pilot report that shows the trusted envelope and failures side by side.
facts.quote: Chapter 13 adds the one-page credibility map and the traffic-light pilot report that shows the trusted envelope and the failures side by side.

facts.text: Reviewers disagree with each other and weigh weaknesses more than strengths.
facts.quote: Reviewers disagree with each other and weigh weaknesses more than strengths

facts.text: The booklet warns that a visual hiding a gap will be found out and recommends showing the gap openly with a plan to close it.
facts.quote: a visual that hides a gap will be found out, and one that shows it openly, with the plan to close it, is the booklet's definition of a visual that works
